 The company continued to maintain a strong operational performance during the quarter. 
EBITDA increased by 39% year -on-year, while EBITDA margins expanded by more than 50 
basis points sequentially to 14.4%, supported by a favourable business mix and continued focus 
on operational efficiencies. 
 Profitability remained robust, with profit after tax reaching a record high of INR 9,900 million, 
representing a 43% year -over-year increase. PAT margins stood at 10 .0% for the quarter, 
reflecting healthy earnings growth and sustained margin resilience. Our financia l position 
remains very strong. 
 Net cash stood at INR 45.2 billion as of September 30th, 2026, compared to INR 29.4 billion a 
year ago. We also witnessed further improvement in our working capital efficiency, with the 
average working capital cycle reducing to approximately 11 days in second quarter fiscal '27. 
This was aided by higher payable days arising from the increased use of letters of credit for our 
raw material procurement. 
 As these benefits gradually normalize, we expect the working capital cycle to trend towards our 
long-term operating range of 45 to 50 days. During the first half of the year, we incurred capital 
expenditures of INR 6.1 billion, reflecting our ongoing investments in capacity expansion, 
supply chain capabilities and future growth platforms. 
 On a half year basis, I am pleased to share that H1 FY27 marked the strongest first half 
performance in the company's history in terms of both top line and profitability.  Revenue grew 
by 46% year-on-year, crossing a significant milestone of INR180 billion. EBITDA increased by 
36% year-on-year, with margins remaining healthy at 14.1%, while profit after tax grew by 38% 
year-on-year, translating into PAT margins of 9.9%. 
 Let me now turn to Slide 6 and discuss the performance of our Wires and Cables business. The 
Wires and Cables segment delivered a strong quarter, recording 47% year -on-year revenue 
growth. Within this, the domestic Wires and Cables business grew by an impressive 50% year -
on-year, driven by healthy demand conditions, strong channel execution and favourable 
commodity linked realizations. 
 We delivered a volume growth of mid -to high single -digit range on top of a strong base from 
the corresponding quarter last year, demonstrating the underlying strength of demand. Within 
the portfolio, wires continued to outpace cables in terms of growth. 
 Channel sales also grew faster than institutional sales, underscoring the resilience and 
effectiveness of our distribution-led model. From a regional perspective, the West remained our 
largest contributor, followed by the South, North and East, highlighti ng the broad-based nature 
of growth across markets. 
 Despite challenging geopolitical environment, exports picked up strongly during the quarter as 
sales grew 17% year-on-year and grew 85% quarter-on-quarter. While exports accounted for a 
relatively lower share of overall revenues, the moderation in contribution is largely attributable 
to the significant faster growth in the domestic market, which expanded the overall revenue base.

We continue to maintain a strong export order pipeline and remain confident about our long term 
growth prospects of this business. 
 EBIT margins in the Wires and Cables segment stood at 14.2%. Margins improved sequentially, 
supported by a favourable product mix and continued operational excellence initiatives. In line 
with our Project Spring roadmap, we remain confident of sustaining medium - to long -term 
EBITDA margins within our guided range of 11% to 13%. 
 Turning now to Slide 8 and our FMEG business. The FMEG segment delivered a breakthrough 
quarter, registering a remarkable 124% year-on-year growth with strong performance across all 
major product categories. 
 Notably, this marks the 11th consecutive quarter of industry leading growth, reflecting the 
effectiveness of our strategy, execution capabilities and strengthening market position. Solar 
products, which constitute the largest category within our FMEG portf olio, continue to be the 
primary growth driver, registering multi-fold growth during this quarter. 
 The segment continues to benefit from favourable structural tailwinds, including the PM Surya 
Ghar Yojana, various state level support programs, and accelerating consumer adoption of 
renewable energy solutions. We remain highly optimistic about the long term oppo rtunity this 
category presents. 
 The broader FMEG portfolio comprising fans, lighting, switches, switchgear, conduits, pipes 
and fittings also delivered healthy growth. Performance was supported by sustained momentum 
in the real estate and construction sectors, alongside our focused effo rts on product innovation, 
distribution expansion, and deeper customer engagement. 
 The segment also achieved a major profitability milestone, with EBIT margins crossing the 
double-digit mark for the first time and recording a 10.1% margin during the quarter. Since 
achieving profitability in Q4 FY25, the business has consistently strengthened its earning profile 
while continuing to invest in talent, product development, innovation, and brand -building 
initiatives. 
 Looking ahead, we remain highly confident about the long-term growth trajectory of the FMEG 
business. Our objective continues to be growing at 1.5x to 2x of the industry growth rate while 
steadily enhancing profitability. Investments in distribution reach, product innovation, category 
expansion, and brand equity will remain central to driving sustainable value creation. 
 Moving to Slide 10 and our EPC business. The EPC segment reported revenues of INR 6,171 
million in Q2 FY27, representing a healthy year-on-year growth of 53%. Segment profitability 
remained strong at INR444 million, translating into an EBIT margin of 7.2%. 
 Over the medium- to long-term, we continue to expect sustainable margins for the EPC business 
to remain in the high single -digit range, supported by disciplined project selection, efficient 
execution, and a healthy order pipeline.

 In closing, I would like to sincerely thank all our stakeholders for their unwavering trust and 
continued support. The performance delivered during the quarter reflects the strength of our 
business model, the commitment of our teams, and the success of our  long-term strategic 
investments. As we look ahead, we remain focused on executing our growth priorities, 
enhancing operational excellence, and creating sustainable value for all our stakeholders. 
 With that, we conclude our prepared remarks and would be happy to take your questions. 
Moderator: Thank you very much. We will now begin the question -and-answer session. The first question 
comes from the line of Kevin Shah with Aditya Birla Money. 
Kevin Shah: And congratulations on a great set of numbers. Firstly, on the FMEG margin. So if you see the 
10.1% is already at the upper end of your projected targets. So could you highlight what are the 
key drivers behind it, and which of these segments are profitable ? Is this solely contributed by 
the solar segment, and would you be looking to revise your Project Spring targets? 
Aditya Nathany: Yes. Thank you, Kevin, for your question. For the FMEG margin question, I think there are few 
things that have worked for us in this quarter and probably the kind of initiatives that we have 
put together over the past few years, and those strategies are actually reaping benefits. 
 Now, definitely scale has increased in this quarter, and as I mentioned in my previous comments, 
all segments in the quarter have actually grown by multifolds, right. Beating the industry growth 
rates. 
 So that's very much a positive sign for us that all the categories are firing at all cylinders with 
kind of the strategies that we are implementing. So that's the first part. I think the scale definitely 
plays an important part, and definitely the operating leverage from here. 
 The second part, I think, to answer to that margin expansion of up to 10.1%, is premium mix has 
also gone up in this quarter for various segments. Today, if you see, the fans mix is around 33% 
in the premium category and the lights also now reaching at 38%. So all of this is actually 
contributing to the margin growth. 
 And the other strategic thing that we have been doing in this segment for the past year or so is 
providing a more solution-driven approach for our portfolio. Today, as you see, as we've already 
mentioned previously in various calls, that the kind of strat egy that we are putting together, 
especially in terms of the building verticals, these FMEG products are actually complementing 
to the way we are approaching the end customers. 
 So it's a kind of bouquet offering that we are doing, and it is reaping benefits for us. I think 
there's a scale. That is why you see the kind of margins that we have generated in FMEG. So all 
these strategies together is reaping benefits because if you se e earlier also, our strategy was 
largely on pan-India basis, right.

 Today, the strategy has moved for regional specific and given the kind of P&L strategy that we 
have for each. That is driving a lot of profitability. The availability of the products in the market 
has improved due tovarious strategic initiatives that we have implemented. 
 Our Polyratna plans that we have put together in the market is also complementing towards this. 
So I think all of this synthesized is getting us the results for FMEG. To answer your second 
question on the growth, I think when we started the Project Spring and we laid ou t our margin

 So over the longer term, I believe we would end up in that kind of a range of 8% to 10% of the

Kevin Shah: Understood. And just a follow-up on the margins. For the Wires and Cables margins also, there 
has been a significant increase there. So can we say that this is mainly led by the channel mix 
improvement? And what are the other drivers? And how much of it do you see it as sustainable

Aditya Nathany: So Kevin, I think when you look at the margins overall, I think it's a confluence of four or five 
things that we have already highlighted in the previous calls. One definitely operating leverage 
has a play into it. 
 If you see our margins, overall margins have expanded around 90 basis points sequentially. So 
there is the operating leverage that is playing in this segment. Definitely, the business mix is 
playing an important part as well, wires have grown far more better than the cables, so that's a 
high accretive margin business for us. 
 Definitely channel has also been better than institutional. So these are four or five things that are 
very important, and if you see the kind of exports growth that we are also having, that is also 
sort of supporting to a certain extent. 
 So I think we are very much happy the way we have delivered , the kind of initiatives that we 
have put together, and it is visible in the results at the moment. And 14.4% overall margins, we 
have Wires and Cable at 14.2%, it is such a remarkable story, Kevin. 
Kevin Shah: Understood. And secondly, in terms of the new suppliers that are coming into the market. So do 
you what is the downside risk that you see to your Project Spring targets in terms of the growth

Aditya Nathany: So Kevin, you need to understand that the guidance that we have provided is for FY30. So it's a

years you may find it at a very high margins, in the double digits. I think we would like to be in 
that guidance range, I think, till FY30, and that's how we continue to maintain our stance of our 
guidance.
